extracted.intended_audience: students of journalism / reporters learning news writing and story analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and question-outline for analyzing and composing news and feature stories, covering lead construction, structure, style, typographical conventions, news-gathering, purpose, and special treatment of fires/accidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary lead contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary lead includes the following details: (1) the persons, (2) the event, (3) the place, (4) the time, (5) the cause, (6) the significant circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any one of these elements of the news may be 'featured' in the place of prominence at the beginning of the story, although the time and the place are seldom played up in this way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature/entertainment story beginning
rubrics_metrics.description: The story of entertainment or appeal usually avoids the summary lead by beginning in one of the ways common to fictitious narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In its beginning, effort to sustain suspense, and semblance of plot the human interest or feature story closely resembles the short story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body arrangement / logical order
rubrics_metrics.description: In the body of the story the details follow a logical order; the arrangement in narrative stories is usually chronological.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only such of the details summarized in the lead are repeated in the body of the story as are needed for clearness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ending / rounding out
rubrics_metrics.description: It is well to round out stories in the last paragraph, though the ending does not receive so much attention as in other prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make-up exigencies often necessitate cutting off the last paragraph or two; keep endings concise and able to be truncated if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary style elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Style of a news story is concerned with such elements as (1) paragraphs, (2) sentences, (3) words; and with such qualities as (1) clearness, (2) force, (3) animation, (4) humor, (5) pathos, (6) taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph & sentence analysis factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis should include (1) the length of the paragraph and of the sentence; (2) the unity of thought in the sentence, and the unity of topic in the paragraph; (3) the coherence, or connection between the parts; and (4) the emphasis given to the important ideas by their position in sentence and paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newspaper paragraph length
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of the narrowness of the columns the newspaper paragraph must be comparatively short to avoid appearing heavy and uninviting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The typical newspaper paragraph contains from 35 to 75 words, whereas the average paragraph in ordinary prose is from 150 to 250 words in length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid involved constructions and long periodic sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: Involved constructions, long periodic sentences, and similar rhetorical devices have no place in journalistic writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such devices tend to prevent rapid reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis by initial position
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis given to an important point by placing it at the beginning of a sentence or a paragraph is a distinctive characteristic of newspaper style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In rapid reading the eye catches important points quickly if they occupy initial positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific, original word choice; avoid unexplained technical terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific words in original combinations are always preferable to colorless, general terms and trite phrases; technical, scientific, and learned words should be avoided unless fully explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slang and colloquial expressions may be used when the tone of the story justifies them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearness and brisk movement
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearness depends upon the arrangement, the connection, and the expression of ideas; how brisk movement and steady progress can be secured is worthy of notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The student should analyze these essential factors in well-written stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of humor and pathos with taste
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor and pathos are not infrequent in news stories, particularly in feature and human interest types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe how humor may be effective without ridicule, buffoonery, or vulgarity, and how offensive facts may be presented without violating canons of good taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical style: consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Peculiarities in details of typographical style such as abbreviation, capitalization, hyphenation, and the use of numerical figures should be noted and each paper has a typographical style of its own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One style is as good as another, but it is essential that consistency be maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical devices for prominence
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant facts may be printed in a box at the beginning or in the body of a story, often in bold-face type; lists of dead and injured, forms for market reports, scores in sports, and similar details have particular arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note the method of arranging and the use of typographical emphasis and why they were used.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Values — paper identification
rubrics_metrics.description: In what paper was the story published?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the paper to understand policy and reader expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Values — paper policy and character
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the policy and the character of the paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the paper's editorial stance or character shapes the treatment of the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Values — circulation reach
rubrics_metrics.description: How widely does the paper circulate outside of the place in which it is published?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circulation scope affects audience expectations and what is 'newsworthy.'

rubrics_metrics.name: News Values — class appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper appeal to a particular class of readers?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the piece is presented from the point of view of that class.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Values — point of view / bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the piece of news presented from the point of view of this class?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how point of view affects framing and emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Values — source of reader interest
rubrics_metrics.description: What, for the average reader, is the source of interest in the news contained in the story?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the hook or elements that attract the average reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Values — degree of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: How much would the news interest the average reader? Why?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate relevance, novelty, proximity, human interest, consequence, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Values — space allocation appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you think that the news was worth more or less space than was given to it? Why?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge proportionality between importance and space.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Values — other significant phases to develop
rubrics_metrics.description: What more significant phases might have been played up or developed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest additional angles or details that would increase news value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of news — origin
rubrics_metrics.description: How did the news originate? Where was the first record of it probably made? By whom?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace the genesis to evaluate reliability and perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of news — records and persons consulted
rubrics_metrics.description: What records and what persons may have been consulted in securing the news?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List likely sources used by the reporter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of news — reference and verification material
rubrics_metrics.description: What reference books or material may have been used in getting or in verifying the details of the story?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess documentary support and verification steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of news — other possible sources
rubrics_metrics.description: What other possible sources might have been consulted?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify additional sources that could have improved accuracy or depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of news-gathering — evidence of methods
rubrics_metrics.description: What evidence does the story give of the methods by which the news was obtained?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for attribution, interviews, documents, on-scene observation, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of news-gathering — completeness of details
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there any evidence that the reporter or correspondent failed to get any of the important details of the piece of news?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge omissions or gaps and whether they affect understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — fairness and bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the story seem to be fair and unbiased?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for slanting, one-sided sourcing, or omitted facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — suppression or coloring of facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there evidence that any important facts were suppressed or that the story was colored to conform to the policy of the paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate editorial influence or censorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — constructive vs destructive handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the handling of the news constructive or destructive in its effect?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the report leads to helpful public awareness or merely sensationalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — writer's constructive purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: What, if any, is the constructive purpose of the writer?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify aims such as reform, warning, praise, or public service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — imitation risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the story so treated as to tempt the reader to imitate anti-social acts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess responsibility regarding potentially harmful descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of story — primary purpose (inform or entertain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the primary purpose of the story to inform or to entertain?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify the piece to judge appropriate style and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of story — narrative/ descriptive/ explanatory/quotation mix
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the story largely narrative and descriptive? Is it largely explanatory? Is it largely direct or indirect quotation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine dominant mode to evaluate structure and sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of story — narrative order
rubrics_metrics.description: If the story is narrative in form, is the order chronological?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity and logic of narrative sequencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of story — narrative clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the narrative clear or confused?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify causes of any confusion: missing facts, poor organization, unclear chronology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of story — narrative pace
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the narrative move slowly or briskly? Why?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate pace to sentence/paragraph length, detail selection, and ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of story — use of eyewitness accounts and quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Are accounts of the event by participants or eye-witnesses used? If so, are these accounts in direct or indirect quotation form?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate reliability and immediacy added by witness material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of story — inclusion of participants' remarks/conversation
rubrics_metrics.description: Are remarks and conversation of participants and eye-witnesses given?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine whether quoted speech adds human interest or clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of story — description detail level
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the description detailed or suggestive? Is it effective? Why?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge descriptive balance between vividness and concision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of story — striving for effect in description
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a striving for effect in the description?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note any overwriting or melodramatic tendencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of story — logical order for speeches/reports
rubrics_metrics.description: If the story is that of a speech, report, etc., is the material arranged in logical order?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess organization for readability and comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of story — human interest emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Is much or little made of the personal, or human interest, element in the story of the speech or the interview?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate balance between factual reporting and human-interest treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure — presence of summary lead or unconventional beginning
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the story a summary lead or an unconventional beginning?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how beginning choice affects reader engagement and information delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure — lead contains essential facts concisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the lead contain the essential facts concisely presented?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether lead gives a clear, compact account of the core of the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure — striking detail played up at opening
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the most striking detail played up as the feature in the first group of words of the opening sentence of the lead?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether opening highlights the most newsworthy element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure — alternative lead elements
rubrics_metrics.description: What other element in the news might have been featured in the lead?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest alternative lead angles and their merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure — lead proportion to whole story
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the lead proportionate in length to the whole story?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess balance between lead length and total coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure — arrangement of details in body
rubrics_metrics.description: How are the details arranged in the body of the story?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify ordering principle and whether it aids comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure — evidence of cutting for makeup
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there any evidence that the story was cut down in making up the paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for abrupt endings, missing transitions, or dangling references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure — paragraph connection
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the paragraphs closely connected?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for transitions and logical flow between paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure — unnecessary repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there unnecessary repetition in the story?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify redundant facts or repeated wording that could be condensed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure — arrangement improvement suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Could the arrangement of the details be improved? How?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose reorganizations to improve clarity or emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary style — paragraph evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the average length of the paragraphs? Are any of the paragraphs too long or too short? Is each paragraph a unit? Are the details well arranged and closely connected in the paragraphs?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: Does the first group of words at the beginning of each paragraph attract the reader as his eye glances down the story? Could any of the paragraph beginnings be made more effective?

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary style — sentence evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the average length of the sentences? Are any of the sentences too long or too short? Is the construction of each sentence evident in rapid reading?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: Is each sentence a unified expression of a closely related group of ideas? Are the parts of the sentences combined in firm, closely knit construction? Do the sentence beginnings attract the reader by the importance and the interest of the ideas expressed? Do any sentences trail off loosely into a succession of phrases and clauses? Is there variety in sentence length and construction?

rubrics_metrics.name: Words — diction and concision
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the style concise or wordy? Is the diction original or hackneyed? Is the style marked by many adjectives or by superlatives? Are the verbs specific and forcible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also evaluate whether the diction is too learned for the comprehension of the average rapid reader; whether words are used idiomatically and accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Words — slang and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Are slang and colloquial expressions found in the story? What is the effect of them? Is the diction in keeping with the tone of the story?

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of style — rapid comprehensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Can the details of the story be easily comprehended in rapid reading; that is, is the style comparatively simple?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess simplicity and immediacy for rapid readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of style — basis of clearness
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon what does the general clearness of the story depend?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify arrangement, connection, expression, and other factors that support clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of style — movement speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the movement slow or rapid? Why?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate movement to sentence structure, paragraphing, and detail selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of style — humor and pathos technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there any humor or pathos in the story? How is the humorous or the pathetic effect secured?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify devices used to achieve emotional effects and whether development is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of style — undeveloped possibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the news possibilities for humorous or pathetic treatment that are not developed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest opportunities for deeper treatment if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of style — good taste
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the story in good taste?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether presentation violates standards of decency or professionalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical style — specific peculiarities
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the peculiarities of abbreviation, capitalization, hyphenation, and use of numerical figures?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note house style and its effect on readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical style — consistency across story
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the typographical style consistent throughout the story?

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical style — prominence by typographical devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Are any details of the story given prominence by typographical devices? If so, why?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether typographical emphasis matches editorial judgment of importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fires & accidents — story type classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Many newspaper reports of fires and accidents may be considered typical examples of narrative and descriptive news stories of the purely informative type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When human life is involved some writers develop the personal or human interest elements while presenting facts fully and accurately; less important incidents may be treated as features if an element lends itself to human-interest treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fires & accidents — constructive vs pandering purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories of fires and accidents, particularly when fatalities occur, may be written so as to be either constructive or destructive in their influence upon readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive effects: emphasize preventive measures, create sympathy for victims, inspire admiration for heroism; stories that pander to ghastly and sensational phases have an unwholesome influence even if factual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fires & accidents — treatment for interest
rubrics_metrics.description: All types of fire and accident stories give opportunity for spirited narrative and vivid description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible means for lending life include accounts of the disaster in direct or indirect quotation, interviews with survivors and eye-witnesses, and conversation between persons involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fires & accidents — important contents to consider
rubrics_metrics.description: Among important details to be considered in analyzing stories of unexpected occurrences are: (1) number of lives lost; (2) number of lives endangered; (3) names of dead and injured; (4) prominent persons and places involved; (5) character and extent of damage; (6) property threatened with damage or destruction; (7) cause and responsibility; (8) investigations; (9) preventive measures against recurrence of event; (10) probable or actual effects; (11) peculiar and unusual circumstances; (12) humorous and pathetic incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any one of these details may be the feature of the story and the space and prominence given are determined by relative news value.
